title: 85. Numeracy & Number Systems: Absolute and Relative Error of Approximations
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the absolute error of an approximation.
questions.question: The exact value of a quantity is \(50\), and its approximation is \(48\). What is the absolute error?
questions.explanation:
The absolute error is the absolute difference between the exact value and the approximation:
\[
\left|50-48\right|=2
\]
Therefore, the absolute error is \(2\). The alternative doubles the absolute difference.
questions.hint: Subtract the approximation from the exact value, then take the absolute value.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the absolute error of a measured length.
questions.question: The exact length of a rod is \(200\text{ cm}\), but it is measured as \(205\text{ cm}\). What is the absolute error of the measurement?
questions.explanation:
The absolute error is
\[
\left|200-205\right|=5\text{ cm}
\]
Therefore, the absolute error is \(5\text{ cm}\). The alternative doubles the absolute difference.
questions.hint: Use the absolute difference between the exact value and the measured value.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the relative error of an approximation as a percentage.
questions.question: The exact value is \(80\), and its approximation is \(76\). What is the relative error, expressed as a percentage?
questions.explanation:
First find the absolute error:
\[
\left|80-76\right|=4
\]
Then divide by the exact value:
\[
\frac{4}{80}=0.05=5\%
\]
Therefore, the relative error is \(5\%\). The alternative reports the absolute error as though it were a percentage.
questions.hint: Relative error is the absolute error divided by the exact value.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the relative error of a mass measurement.
questions.question: The exact mass of an object is \(250\text{ g}\), but it is measured as \(240\text{ g}\). What is the relative error, expressed as a percentage?
questions.explanation:
The absolute error is
\[
\left|250-240\right|=10\text{ g}
\]
The relative error is
\[
\frac{10}{250}=0.04=4\%
\]
Therefore, the relative error is \(4\%\). The alternative uses the measured value as the denominator: \(\frac{10}{240}\approx 4.17\%\). Relative error uses the exact value \(250\).
questions.hint: Divide the absolute error by the exact mass, then convert to a percentage.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the relative error of a length approximation.
questions.question: The exact length is \(12.5\text{ m}\), and its approximation is \(12.2\text{ m}\). What is the relative error, expressed as a percentage?
questions.explanation:
The absolute error is
\[
\left|12.5-12.2\right|=0.3\text{ m}
\]
The relative error is
\[
\frac{0.3}{12.5}=0.024=2.4\%
\]
Therefore, the relative error is \(2.4\%\). The alternative divides by the approximation: \(\frac{0.3}{12.2}\approx 2.46\%\). The required denominator is the exact length \(12.5\).
questions.hint: Find the absolute error first, then decide which of the two lengths belongs in the denominator.

questions.concept: Relative Error with a Decimal Exact Value
questions.learningObjective: Calculate relative error using the exact value as the denominator and express it as a percentage.
questions.question: The exact value is \(3.6\), and its approximation is \(3.8\). What is the relative error, expressed as a percentage? Round the percentage to two decimal places.
questions.explanation:
The absolute error is
\[
\left|3.6-3.8\right|=0.2
\]
The relative error is
\[
\frac{0.2}{3.6}=0.0555\ldots\approx 5.56\%
\]
Therefore, the relative error is approximately \(5.56\%\). The alternative uses the approximation as the denominator.
questions.hint: Divide the absolute error by \(3.6\), then multiply by \(100\%\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine which approximation has the smaller absolute error.
questions.question: The exact value is \(60\). Approximation P is \(58\), and Approximation Q is \(61\). Which approximation has the smaller absolute error?
questions.explanation:
For Approximation P, the absolute error is
\[
\left|60-58\right|=2
\]
For Approximation Q, the absolute error is
\[
\left|60-61\right|=1
\]
Since \(1<2\), Approximation Q has the smaller absolute error.
questions.hint: Compute the absolute error for each approximation and compare the results.

questions.learningObjective: Determine which approximation has the smaller relative error.
questions.question: Approximation P estimates an exact value of \(200\) by \(190\). Approximation Q estimates an exact value of \(50\) by \(46\). Which has the smaller relative error?
questions.explanation: For P, the absolute error is \(10\), so its relative error is \(\frac{10}{200}=5\%\). For Q, the absolute error is \(4\), so its relative error is \(\frac{4}{50}=8\%\). Thus P has the smaller relative error even though its absolute error is larger. Comparing absolute errors alone would incorrectly select Q.
questions.hint: Divide each absolute error by its own exact value before comparing.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate relative error using the exact value as the denominator and express it as a percentage.
questions.question: The exact value is \(45\), and its approximation is \(42\). What is the relative error, expressed as a percentage? Round the percentage to two decimal places.
questions.explanation:
The absolute error is
\[
\left|45-42\right|=3
\]
The relative error is
\[
\frac{3}{45}=\frac{1}{15}=0.0666\ldots\approx 6.67\%
\]
Therefore, the relative error is approximately \(6.67\%\). The alternative divides the error by the approximation: \(\frac{3}{42}\approx 7.14\%\). Relative error uses the exact value as its denominator.
questions.hint: Divide the absolute error by the exact value \(45\).

questions.concept: Relative Error in a Practical Measurement
questions.learningObjective: Calculate relative error using the exact value as the denominator and express it as a percentage.
questions.question: The exact length is \(8.0\text{ cm}\), and its approximation is \(7.6\text{ cm}\). What is the relative error, expressed as a percentage?
questions.explanation:
The absolute error is
\[
\left|8.0-7.6\right|=0.4\text{ cm}
\]
The relative error is
\[
\frac{0.4}{8.0}=0.05=5\%
\]
Therefore, the relative error is \(5\%\). The decimal ratio \(0.05\) is \(5\%\), not \(0.05\%\); the alternative omits the conversion to a percentage.
questions.hint: Use the exact length \(8.0\text{ cm}\) as the denominator.
